title: Cyclone Akvan to Hit Andhra Coast Friday With Winds up to 145 Kmph
excerpt: The IMD expects Akvan to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20, with seven Andhra districts on red alert and Odisha evacuating vulnerable villages.
body:
• Cyclone Akvan lay over the Bay of Bengal on Wednesday morning, about 580 km east of Chennai, and is moving slowly north at about 3 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
  • The IMD expects Akvan to become a severe cyclonic storm on Wednesday, November 18, a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning, and to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on Friday, November 20, between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, with winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph.
  • Seven Andhra Pradesh districts are on red alert, Odisha has deployed 74 rescue teams and begun evacuating vulnerable residents in its southern districts, and Tamil Nadu has told fishermen to stay ashore.
  • For families in the storm's path: the IMD has warned of storm surge of 0.4 to 1.2 metres above the tide in low-lying areas of Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada and Visakhapatnam districts around landfall, and of isolated extremely heavy rain over coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20.

Cyclone Akvan is closing on India's east coast, and the India Meteorological Department's forecast gives coastal Andhra Pradesh roughly two days to prepare before a very severe cyclonic storm crosses the coast around noon on Friday, November 20.

At 5:30 a.m. IST on Wednesday, November 18, the storm was centred about 580 km east of Chennai, 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 730 km south of Gopalpur, moving north at about 3 kmph, according to the IMD update carried in live coverage of the storm. The IMD has issued a cyclone alert — an orange message — for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.

The forecast track

"Northern Tamil Nadu districts including Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu may see moderate to heavy rain with thunder and gusty winds on November 18 and 19."

The IMD's national bulletin expects Akvan to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal by Wednesday evening, then turn northwest and strengthen further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning, November 19. It is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts around noon on Friday, November 20, at very severe intensity, with maximum sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, before weakening over land.

Rainfall is the second threat. The IMD expects heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places over coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20, with isolated extremely heavy falls of 21 cm or more; heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Odisha from November 19 to 21; heavy rain at isolated places in north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on November 19; and heavy rain in eastern Telangana on November 20 and 21. Northern Tamil Nadu districts including Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu may see moderate to heavy rain with thunder and gusty winds on November 18 and 19.

States are moving before the storm does

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday directed officials to take precautionary measures for the coastal regions expected to be affected on November 20, according to PTI. The IMD has issued a red alert for seven Andhra districts, among them Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla.

Odisha stepped up preparations on Monday, deploying 74 rescue teams and starting early evacuation of vulnerable residents in its southern districts, PTI reported. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the government had made "full arrangements to secure lives and property," while Manorama Mohanty, director of the Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre, said Odisha was likely to face a lower impact from Akvan than from Cyclone Arnab. The Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department has issued an urgent advisory asking fishermen to suspend all fishing and remain ashore in rough seas.

Third storm in three weeks

Akvan is the third cyclonic system to form in the region within three weeks, following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. The name Akvan was contributed by Iran under the WMO/ESCAP tropical cyclone naming system. At least 11 people were killed during Cyclone Arnab in Odisha, PTI reported — a measure of why state governments along this coast evacuate early rather than late.

What this means for you

If your family is in coastal Andhra Pradesh, southern Odisha or north Tamil Nadu, the decision window is now, not Friday: the landfall zone between Nellore and Visakhapatnam faces the strongest winds and the forecast storm surge around midday on November 20, and the heaviest rain arrives a day earlier. Follow the IMD's bulletins rather than social-media track maps, keep phones charged, and expect travel through the landfall districts to be disrupted around the crossing window. The IMD updates its national bulletin through the day as the track firms up.
